novel.justification: Strict positivity is imposed only for the fixed-instance sharp converse and quantitative conditioning. Uniqueness and sufficiency hold on the published positive-semidefinite class; an ambiguity in this positive-definite subclass proves minimax sharpness over the larger class without asserting ambiguity at every singular boundary instance.

assumptions.condition: \(s_{ek}\ge0\) for every \(e\in H\) and \(1\le k\le p\).

standard.name: Population BACKSHIFT covariance equation, with the invariant-noise cone stated separately.

assumptions.condition: \(s_{ek}=Z_{ek}a_{ek}\) for every \(e\in H\) and \(1\le k\le p\).

novel.justification: The prespecified-support factorization is a proposal-specific restriction that conditions on an investigator-chosen sparse intervention design. It is realistic in multi-environment experiments whose intervention targets are fixed before continuously distributed positive doses are assigned.

assumptions.condition: The joint law of \((a_{ek}:e\in H,1\le k\le p,Z_{ek}=1)\) is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure on its positive orthant.

novel.justification: Joint absolute continuity conditional on a fixed sparse support pattern is a genericity condition for nonzero intervention strengths. It is satisfied when active intervention variances have a joint density on the positive orthant, including independently randomized positive strengths and correlated continuously distributed dose designs.

definitions.name: Mkl
definitions.construction: For \(1\le k<\ell\le p\), \(M_{k\ell}=\max_{L\subset\mathbb R^2\,\mathrm{affine\ line}}\#\{e\in H:(s_{ek},s_{e\ell})\in L\}\).

definitions.name: Rc
definitions.construction: For \(\Sigma\in(\mathbb S_{+}^{p})^{E}\), \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)=\{A\in\mathcal D:\exists K\subseteq E,\ |K|\ge h,\ \exists\Psi\in\mathbb S_{+}^p,\ \exists t_e\in[0,\infty)^p,\ \Sigma_e=A^{-1}(\Psi+\operatorname{diag}(t_e))A^{-\mathsf T}\ \forall e\in K\}\).

definitions.name: gamma
definitions.construction: Set \(\gamma_H=0\) when \(h-c<3\); otherwise set \(\gamma_H=\min_{1\le k<\ell\le p}\min_{S\subseteq H,\,|S|=h-c}\max_{e<f<g\in S}\left|\det\begin{pmatrix}1&s_{ek}&s_{e\ell}\\1&s_{fk}&s_{f\ell}\\1&s_{gk}&s_{g\ell}\end{pmatrix}\right|\).

definitions.name: SubsetConsensus
definitions.construction: Definitional implementation note: given a feasibility oracle that returns the full solution set for each queried semialgebraic system, query every \(K\subseteq E\) with \(|K|=h\) for all \(A\in\mathcal D\) satisfying \(\operatorname{offdiag}(A(\Sigma_e-\Sigma_f)A^{\mathsf T})=0\) for \(e,f\in K\) and admitting one \(\Psi\in\mathbb S_{+}^p\) with nonnegative diagonal shifts for the transformed raw covariances. Define \(\text{SubsetConsensus}(\Sigma,c)\) as the union of the oracle-returned solution sets. This enumeration makes exactly \(\binom{m}{h}\) oracle queries and, by expansion of \(\text{def:compatible-set}\), its returned union equals \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)\); neither fact is a theorem contribution or a claim that an encoded terminating solver is supplied.

definitions.name: rRadius
definitions.construction: \(r_{n,\alpha,H}=\max_{e\in H}\sup_{\Gamma\in\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}}\|\Gamma-\Sigma_e\|_{\mathrm{op}}\in[0,+\infty]\), where the supremum and hence the maximum may equal \(+\infty\).

definitions.name: diamOp
definitions.construction: For every nonempty matrix set \(\mathcal A\), \(\operatorname{diam}_{\mathrm{op}}(\mathcal A)=\sup_{A_1,A_2\in\mathcal A}\|A_1-A_2\|_{\mathrm{op}}\in[0,+\infty]\).

definitions.name: outerOp
definitions.construction: For every nonempty matrix set \(\mathcal A\) and matrix \(D\), \(\operatorname{outer}_{\mathrm{op}}(\mathcal A,D)=\sup_{A_1\in\mathcal A}\|A_1-D\|_{\mathrm{op}}\in[0,+\infty]\).

definitions.name: RegionCode
definitions.construction:
A rational semialgebraic region code in dimension \(p\) is a finite list of polynomials in the \(p(p+1)/2\) independent entries of a symmetric matrix \(G\), with coefficients in \(\mathbb Q\), together with a finite Boolean formula \(\rho(G)\) whose atoms are comparisons of those polynomials with zero. Its realization is
\[
\operatorname{Real}(\rho)
=\{G\in\mathbb S_{++}^p:\rho(G)\}.
\]
An encoded covariance-region family supplies, for every \(n\geq1\), \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), and \(e\in E\), such a finite code \(\rho^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}\) and requires
\[
\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}
=\operatorname{Real}\bigl(\rho^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}\bigr)\neq\varnothing.
\]
The code may be random through the sample, but after a sample outcome is fixed it is a finite rational string and its displayed equality with the region is exact, not an outer approximation or a membership oracle.

definitions.name: Ualpha
definitions.construction:
For each \(n\geq1\) and \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), let \(\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}\) be the nonempty realization of its code in \(\text{def:encoded-covariance-regions}\). Define
\[
\mathcal U^{(n)}_{\alpha}
=\bigcup_{\substack{\Gamma_e\in\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}\\ e\in E}}
\mathcal R_c(\Gamma).
\]
Thus \(\mathcal U^{(n)}_{\alpha}\) is the set-valued inversion of the encoded simultaneous covariance regions through the population replacement-compatibility map \(\mathcal R_c\). Coverage, computability, margin auditing, and singleton conclusions are theorem properties and are not included in this construction definition.

definitions.name: CertificateInferenceHandle
definitions.construction:
Fix a realized encoded region family, \(n\geq1\), \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), and rational thresholds \(\gamma_0,\zeta_0,\lambda_0>0\) and \(\overline\kappa,\overline M\geq1\). For each \(K\subseteq E\) with \(|K|=h\), introduce a candidate tuple
\[
w=(K,A,\Psi,(t_e)_{e\in K},(\Gamma_e)_{e\in K}).
\]
The full feasibility formula \(F_K(w)\) is the conjunction of: each encoded region formula at \(\Gamma_e\); \(\Gamma_e\in\mathbb S_{++}^p\); \(A_{ii}=1\); \((\det A)^2>0\); \(1-\pi_C(A)>0\) and \(1+\pi_C(A)>0\) for every directed simple cycle \(C\), where \(\pi_C(A)\) is the corresponding entry product in \(I_p-A\); \(\Psi\in\mathbb S_+^p\); \(t_{ej}\geq0\); and
\[
A\Gamma_eA^{\mathsf T}=\Psi+\operatorname{diag}(t_e)
\qquad(e\in K).
\]
For such a tuple set \(\zeta(w)=1-\max_C|\pi_C(A)|\), \(\kappa(w)=\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|A^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\),
\[
\lambda(w)=\min\left\{\lambda_{\min}(\Psi),\min_{e\in K}\lambda_{\min}(\Gamma_e)\right\},
\qquad
M(w)=1+\|\Psi\|_{\mathrm{op}}+\max_{e\in K}\|\Gamma_e\|_{\mathrm{op}}+\max_{e\in K}\|\operatorname{diag}(t_e)\|_{\mathrm{op}},
\]
and, writing
\[
\Delta^{k\ell}_{efg}(t)=
\det\begin{pmatrix}
1&t_{ek}&t_{e\ell}\\
1&t_{fk}&t_{f\ell}\\
1&t_{gk}&t_{g\ell}
\end{pmatrix},
\]
set \(\gamma(w)=0\) if \(h-c<3\), and otherwise set
\[
\gamma(w)=
\min_{1\leq k<\ell\leq p}
\min_{\substack{S\subseteq K\\|S|=h-c}}
\max_{e<f<g\in S}|\Delta^{k\ell}_{efg}(t)|.
\]
The certificate procedure forms
\[
\Phi_{\mathcal U}(A)
=\bigvee_{\substack{K\subseteq E\\|K|=h}}
\exists\Psi\,\exists(t_e)_{e\in K}\,\exists(\Gamma_e)_{e\in K} F_K(w),
\]
calls effective real quantifier elimination to obtain a quantifier-free rational-polynomial code in \(A\), and calls it again on the closed sentence asserting that some feasible tuple violates at least one of
\[
\gamma(w)\geq\gamma_0,\qquad
\zeta(w)\geq\zeta_0,\qquad
\lambda(w)\geq\lambda_0,\qquad
\kappa(w)\leq\overline\kappa,\qquad
M(w)\leq\overline M.
\]
It returns the code for \(\Phi_{\mathcal U}\) when that sentence is false and returns \(\mathsf{ABSTAIN}\) when it is true. This definition names the finite symbolic procedure and its candidate margins; exactness, termination, coverage, and the abstention guarantee are asserted only by the theorem.

statements.statement: Let the first explanation \(D^{(1)},H_1,s^{(1)}\) and the second explanation \(D^{(2)},H_2,s^{(2)}\) fit the same \(\Sigma\), each through a BACKSHIFT covariance equation satisfying the unit-diagonal and cycle-product normalization, with its own invariant positive-semidefinite nuisance, nonnegative shifts, and \(|H_r|\ge h=m-c\). Set \(J=H_1\cap H_2\). Then \(|J|\ge m-2c=h-c\). If, for every \(k<\ell\), the first explanation's cloud \(\{(s^{(1)}_{ek},s^{(1)}_{e\ell}):e\in J\}\) is not contained in an affine line, then \(D^{(1)}=D^{(2)}\).
statements.justification: This isolates the new robust step: competing explanations share only \(m-2c\) slots, on which ordinary congruence-diagonalizer uniqueness must be normalized causally.
statements.gap: RothenhauslerEtAl2015BackShift, Theorem 1, and KleinsteuberShen2013NUJDUniqueness, Theorem 1, treat a fixed complete diagonalizable family rather than the intersection of two adversarially selected families.
statements.consumer: The lemma supplies the sufficiency half of the exact replacement-radius theorem after two candidate honest sets lose different slots.
statements.proof_tex:
For \(r\in\{1,2\}\), let \(\Psi^{(r)}\in\mathbb S_+^p\) be the invariant nuisance in the \(r\)-th fitted BACKSHIFT equation.  The fitting hypotheses give
\[
 D^{(r)}\Sigma_eD^{(r)\mathsf T}
 =\Psi^{(r)}+\operatorname{diag}(s^{(r)}_e),
 \qquad e\in H_r.
 \tag{1}
\]
Because \(H_1,H_2\subseteq E\), \(|E|=m\), and \(|H_r|\ge h=m-c\), inclusion--exclusion gives
\[
 |J|=|H_1\cap H_2|
 =|H_1|+|H_2|-|H_1\cup H_2|
 \ge 2h-m=m-2c=h-c.
 \tag{2}
\]

Set \(Q=D^{(2)}(D^{(1)})^{-1}\).  The noncollinearity hypothesis implies that \(J\) is nonempty, since every set of at most two points in \(\mathbb R^2\) is contained in an affine line.  Fix \(e_0\in J\).  For \(e\in J\), subtract (1) at \(e_0\) from (1) at \(e\) in each explanation and use \(D^{(2)}=QD^{(1)}\).  With
\[
 x_e=s^{(1)}_e-s^{(1)}_{e_0},
 \qquad
 y_e=s^{(2)}_e-s^{(2)}_{e_0},
\]
this gives
\[
 Q\operatorname{diag}(x_e)Q^{\mathsf T}
 =\operatorname{diag}(y_e),
 \qquad e\in J.
 \tag{3}
\]
Let \(W=\operatorname{span}\{x_e:e\in J\}\subseteq\mathbb R^p\).  By linearity of (3),
\[
 Q\operatorname{diag}(w)Q^{\mathsf T}
 \text{ is diagonal for every }w\in W.
 \tag{4}
\]

For each \(k<\ell\), the coordinate projection of \(W\) onto coordinates \(k,\ell\) is all of \(\mathbb R^2\).  Otherwise that projection would have dimension at most one, so there would be a nonzero \((u,v)\in\mathbb R^2\) satisfying
\[
 u(s^{(1)}_{ek}-s^{(1)}_{e_0k})
 +v(s^{(1)}_{e\ell}-s^{(1)}_{e_0\ell})=0
 \quad\text{for every }e\in J.
 \tag{5}
\]
Equation (5) would put the entire \((k,\ell)\)-cloud on the affine line through \((s^{(1)}_{e_0k},s^{(1)}_{e_0\ell})\) with normal \((u,v)\), contradicting the hypothesis.

Choose a basis \(w^1,\ldots,w^d\) of \(W\), where \(d=\dim(W)\), and define the coordinate profiles
\[
 u_k=(w^1_k,\ldots,w^d_k)^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^d,
 \qquad 1\le k\le p.
\]
The projection conclusion says that \(u_k,u_\ell\) are linearly independent whenever \(k\ne\ell\); in particular, each \(u_k\) is nonzero.  Choose \(\beta\in\mathbb R^d\) outside the finitely many proper hyperplanes \(\{\beta:\beta^{\mathsf T}u_k=0\}\).  Having fixed \(\beta\), choose \(\alpha\in\mathbb R^d\) outside the finitely many hyperplanes
\[
 \left\{\alpha:
 \alpha^{\mathsf T}\bigl((\beta^{\mathsf T}u_\ell)u_k
 -(\beta^{\mathsf T}u_k)u_\ell\bigr)=0\right\},
 \qquad k<\ell.
 \tag{6}
\]
Each normal vector in (6) is nonzero: if it vanished, the nonzero scalars \(\beta^{\mathsf T}u_k\) and \(\beta^{\mathsf T}u_\ell\) would make \(u_k,u_\ell\) proportional.  These choices exist because a finite union of proper linear hyperplanes cannot cover \(\mathbb R^d\).  For completeness, the product of their nonzero defining linear forms is a nonzero polynomial; induction on the number of variables, using the one-variable root bound, shows that a nonzero real polynomial cannot vanish everywhere.

Put
\[
 b=\sum_{j=1}^d\beta_jw^j,
 \qquad
 a=\sum_{j=1}^d\alpha_jw^j,
 \qquad
 \rho_k=\frac{a_k}{b_k}.
\]
The choice of \(\beta\) gives \(b_k\ne0\) for every \(k\), and (6) gives \(\rho_k\ne\rho_\ell\) for \(k\ne\ell\).  By (4), both
\[
 G=Q\operatorname{diag}(a)Q^{\mathsf T}
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 K=Q\operatorname{diag}(b)Q^{\mathsf T}
\]
are diagonal.  Moreover, \(K\) is invertible because \(Q\) and \(\operatorname{diag}(b)\) are invertible.  Hence
\[
 GK^{-1}
 =Q\operatorname{diag}(\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_p)Q^{-1}
 \tag{7}
\]
is diagonal.  Its eigenvalues are the pairwise distinct numbers \(\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_p\), so every eigenspace of the diagonal matrix on the left of (7) is a coordinate axis.  The columns of \(Q\), which are the corresponding eigenvectors on the right, are therefore supported on coordinate axes.  Invertibility then makes \(Q\) monomial: there are a permutation \(\pi\) and nonzero scalars \(q_i\) such that
\[
 Q_{i,\pi(i)}=q_i,
 \qquad Q_{ij}=0\quad(j\ne\pi(i)).
 \tag{8}
\]

It remains to remove this monomial ambiguity.  By \(\text{def:admissible-matrices}\), both fitted structural matrices have unit diagonal and satisfy the strict cycle-product bound.  From \(D^{(2)}=QD^{(1)}\), (8), and the unit diagonals,
\[
 1=D^{(2)}_{ii}=q_iD^{(1)}_{\pi(i),i}.
 \tag{9}
\]
If \(\pi\) had a nontrivial cycle \(i_1,\ldots,i_r\), where \(r\ge2\) and \(\pi(i_t)=i_{t+1}\) cyclically, (9) would imply
\[
 \prod_{t=1}^r\left|D^{(1)}_{i_{t+1},i_t}\right|
 =\prod_{t=1}^r|q_{i_t}|^{-1}.
 \tag{10}
\]
The entries on the left of (10), up to signs, form a directed simple cycle of \(I_p-D^{(1)}\).  On the other hand,
\[
 D^{(2)}_{i_t,i_{t+1}}
 =q_{i_t}D^{(1)}_{i_{t+1},i_{t+1}}=q_{i_t},
\]
so these entries, again up to signs, form the reverse directed simple cycle of \(I_p-D^{(2)}\).  The two strict cycle-product inequalities in \(\text{def:admissible-matrices}\) would therefore give
\[
 \prod_{t=1}^r|q_{i_t}|^{-1}<1
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \prod_{t=1}^r|q_{i_t}|<1,
\]
whose product is the contradiction \(1<1\).  Thus \(\pi\) is the identity.  Equation (9) and \(D^{(1)}_{ii}=1\) then give \(q_i=1\) for every \(i\).  Hence \(Q=I_p\) and \(D^{(1)}=D^{(2)}\).

statements.statement: Fix an honest BACKSHIFT instance \(D,H,s,\Omega\) with \(D\in\mathcal D\), nonnegative shifts, \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_{+}^{p}\), and \(\Sigma_e=D^{-1}(\Omega+\operatorname{diag}(s_e))D^{-\mathsf T}\) for every \(e\in H\). If \(\delta_H>c\), equivalently \(\gamma_H>0\), then \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)=\{D\}\) for every assignment of matrices in \(\mathbb S_{+}^{p}\) to the \(c\) slots in \(E\setminus H\). If, in addition, this fixed instance has \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_{++}^{p}\) and \(\delta_H\le c\), then there are positive-definite values for all slots in \(E\setminus H\), a matrix \(D'\in\mathcal D\) with \(D'\ne D\), an invariant \(\Omega'\in\mathbb S_{++}^{p}\), and nonnegative shifts on a set \(H'\subseteq E\) with \(|H'|=h\) such that \(D,D'\in\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)\). Consequently, over the published class allowing \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_{+}^{p}\) and positive-semidefinite covariance slots, the threshold \(\delta_H>c\) is minimax sharp: whenever \(\delta_H\le c\), the class contains an ambiguity witness in its positive-definite invariant-noise and covariance subclass. No ambiguity is asserted for every fixed singular boundary value of \(\Omega\). On the positive-definite invariant-noise interior and at \(c=0\), the equivalence is exactly the BACKSHIFT pairwise noncollinearity criterion.
statements.justification: The theorem gives full published-class sufficiency and the exact minimax number of whole covariance environments that population BACKSHIFT can lose, with pointwise necessity stated only where its interior deformation is valid.
statements.gap: Published BACKSHIFT gives the all-honest criterion, while threshold-trimming joint diagonalization does not provide a worst-case whole-slot replacement radius, a legal contamination, or the distinction between boundary sufficiency and interior pointwise necessity.
statements.consumer: Investigators obtain an exact design audit: passing the distance test certifies every positive-semidefinite covariance assignment, while failing it rules out a uniform class guarantee through an explicit positive-definite ambiguity witness.
statements.proof_tex:
The causal substrate is the linear equilibrium model encoded by \(\text{ass:honest-covariance-model}\).  Its structural target is \(D\), and hence \(B=I_p-D\); the observed-law recovery map is the set \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)\) in \(\text{def:compatible-set}\).  We prove their equality under the stated conditions rather than defining the causal target through that observable map.

First suppose \(\delta_H>c\), and fix an arbitrary assignment of positive-semidefinite matrices to the \(c\) slots in \(E\setminus H\).  By \(\text{ass:honest-covariance-model}\), \(\text{ass:nonnegative-shifts}\), the premise \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_+^p\), and \(D\in\mathcal D\) from \(\text{ass:backshift-normalization}\), the choices
\[
 K=H,
 \qquad \Psi=\Omega,
 \qquad t_e=s_e
\]
satisfy every constraint in \(\text{def:compatible-set}\).  Thus \(D\in\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)\).  This step uses neither invertibility of an honest covariance nor invertibility of a replacement covariance.

Take any \(A\in\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)\).  By \(\text{def:compatible-set}\), there are \(K\subseteq E\), \(|K|\ge h\), \(\Psi\in\mathbb S_+^p\), and \(t_e\in[0,\infty)^p\) such that
\[
 \Sigma_e=A^{-1}\bigl(\Psi+\operatorname{diag}(t_e)\bigr)A^{-\mathsf T},
 \qquad e\in K.
 \tag{11}
\]
For \(J=H\cap K\), inclusion--exclusion, \(|E|=m\), and \(|H|=h=m-c\) give
\[
 |J|\ge |H|+|K|-m\ge2h-m=h-c.
 \tag{12}
\]
By \(\text{def:environment-distance}\) and \(\text{def:max-line-occupancy}\),
\[
 \delta_H>c
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 M_{k\ell}<h-c
 \quad\text{for every }1\le k<\ell\le p.
 \tag{13}
\]
If the indexed points \(\{(s_{ek},s_{e\ell}):e\in J\}\) lay on an affine line for some \(k<\ell\), that line would contain at least \(|J|\ge h-c\) honest indices, contradicting (13).  Thus every pairwise cloud on \(J\) is noncollinear.  Equations (11) and \(\text{ass:honest-covariance-model}\), together with the positive-semidefinite nuisances \(\Psi,\Omega\), the nonnegative shifts \(t_e,s_e\), and \(A,D\in\mathcal D\), verify the premises of \(\text{lem:overlap-uniqueness}\).  That lemma yields \(A=D\).  Hence
\[
 \mathcal R_c(\Sigma)=\{D\}.
 \tag{14}
\]
No value of a slot outside \(H\) entered the argument, so (14) holds for every positive-semidefinite replacement assignment, including singular assignments.

We next compare the deletion distance with the affine-minor margin.  Put \(q=h-c\).  Any indexed family of \(h\) points has at least \(\min(2,h)\) indices on one affine line, so
\[
 M_{k\ell}\ge\min(2,h).
 \tag{15}
\]
Consequently (13) is impossible when \(q<3\), exactly the regime in which \(\text{def:affine-separation}\) sets \(\gamma_H=0\).  Suppose \(q\ge3\).  For fixed \(S\subseteq H\) with \(|S|=q\), the points \((s_{ek},s_{e\ell})\), \(e\in S\), lie on an affine line if and only if the matrix having rows \((1,s_{ek},s_{e\ell})\) has rank at most two.  By the elementary rank criterion, this is equivalent to vanishing of every minor
\[
 \det\begin{pmatrix}
 1&s_{ek}&s_{e\ell}\\
 1&s_{fk}&s_{f\ell}\\
 1&s_{gk}&s_{g\ell}
 \end{pmatrix},
 \qquad e<f<g,\quad e,f,g\in S.
 \tag{16}
\]
All sets of indices involved are finite.  Therefore the finite minimum in \(\text{def:affine-separation}\) is positive exactly when, for every pair \(k<\ell\), every \(q\)-element subset contains a triple with nonzero determinant.  Equivalently, no affine line contains \(q\) honest indices.  Thus
\[
 \gamma_H>0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 M_{k\ell}<q\ \text{for every }k<\ell
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \delta_H>c.
 \tag{17}
\]

It remains to prove the pointwise converse under the additional local condition \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_{++}^p\).  Assume \(\delta_H\le c\) and retain \(q=h-c=m-2c\).

First suppose \(q\le0\).  Then \(|E\setminus H|=c\ge h\), so choose \(H'\subseteq E\setminus H\) with \(|H'|=h\).  Fix \(k<\ell\), let \(F_{k\ell}\) be the matrix whose only nonzero entry is a one in position \((k,\ell)\), and put
\[
 D'_{\varepsilon}=D+\varepsilon F_{k\ell}.
 \tag{18}
\]
For every nonzero \(\varepsilon\), this matrix differs from \(D\) and retains unit diagonal.  Since the determinant is continuous and \(D\) is invertible, \(D'_{\varepsilon}\) remains invertible for all sufficiently small \(|\varepsilon|\).  Moreover, \(\operatorname{CP}(I_p-A)\) is the maximum of finitely many absolute cycle-product polynomials in the entries of \(A\), hence is continuous.  The strict bound \(\operatorname{CP}(I_p-D)<1\) therefore persists for sufficiently small \(|\varepsilon|\).  Choose such a nonzero \(\varepsilon\), set \(D'=D'_{\varepsilon}\in\mathcal D\), and set \(\Omega'=I_p\in\mathbb S_{++}^p\).  For every \(e\in E\setminus H\), assign
\[
 \Sigma_e=(D')^{-1}\Omega'(D')^{-\mathsf T}.
 \tag{19}
\]
Each matrix in (19) is positive definite by invertible congruence.  The original explanation fits \(H\), while \((D',\Omega')\) with zero shifts fits \(H'\).  Hence \(D,D'\in\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)\).

Now suppose \(q>0\).  By \(\delta_H\le c\), \(\text{def:environment-distance}\), and \(\text{def:max-line-occupancy}\), there exist \(k<\ell\), an affine line \(L\), and a set \(S\subseteq H\) with \(|S|=q\) such that all \((s_{ek},s_{e\ell})\), \(e\in S\), lie on \(L\).  Choose a nonzero direction \(v=(v_k,v_\ell)\) of \(L\), fix \(e_0\in S\), and define \(\tau_e\in\mathbb R\) by
\[
 (s_{ek}-s_{e_0k},s_{e\ell}-s_{e_0\ell})
 =\tau_e(v_k,v_\ell),
 \qquad e\in S.
 \tag{20}
\]
For real \(\varepsilon\), put
\[
 \eta_k(\varepsilon)=1+\varepsilon v_kD_{\ell k},
 \qquad
 \eta_\ell(\varepsilon)=1-\varepsilon v_\ell D_{k\ell},
 \tag{21}
\]
and let \(Q_\varepsilon\) equal the identity outside its \(k,\ell\) principal block, where
\[
 (Q_\varepsilon)_{\{k,\ell\},\{k,\ell\}}
 =\begin{pmatrix}
 \eta_k(\varepsilon)^{-1}&\varepsilon v_k\eta_k(\varepsilon)^{-1}\\
 -\varepsilon v_\ell\eta_\ell(\varepsilon)^{-1}&\eta_\ell(\varepsilon)^{-1}
 \end{pmatrix}.
 \tag{22}
\]
At \(\varepsilon=0\), both denominators and \(\det(Q_\varepsilon)\) equal one, so all are nonzero in a neighborhood of zero.  Define \(D'_{\varepsilon}=Q_\varepsilon D\).  Since \(D_{kk}=D_{\ell\ell}=1\), direct multiplication gives
\[
 (D'_{\varepsilon})_{kk}
 =\frac{1+\varepsilon v_kD_{\ell k}}{\eta_k(\varepsilon)}=1,
 \qquad
 (D'_{\varepsilon})_{\ell\ell}
 =\frac{1-\varepsilon v_\ell D_{k\ell}}{\eta_\ell(\varepsilon)}=1,
 \tag{23}
\]
and all other diagonal entries remain one.  The determinant and cycle-product continuity argument used after (18) shows that \(D'_{\varepsilon}\in\mathcal D\) for all sufficiently small \(|\varepsilon|\).  Because \(v\ne0\), at least one off-diagonal entry in (22) is nonzero for every sufficiently small nonzero \(\varepsilon\); hence \(Q_\varepsilon\ne I_p\) and \(D'_{\varepsilon}\ne D\).

For \(x_e=s_e-s_{e_0}\), direct multiplication of the block in (22), followed by (20), gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \relax[Q_\varepsilon\operatorname{diag}(x_e)Q_\varepsilon^{\mathsf T}]_{k\ell}
 &=\frac{-\varepsilon v_\ell x_{ek}+\varepsilon v_kx_{e\ell}}
 {\eta_k(\varepsilon)\eta_\ell(\varepsilon)}\\
 &=\frac{-\varepsilon v_\ell\tau_ev_k+\varepsilon v_k\tau_ev_\ell}
 {\eta_k(\varepsilon)\eta_\ell(\varepsilon)}=0.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{24}
\]
Every other off-diagonal entry vanishes because \(Q_\varepsilon\) is block diagonal with an identity complement.  Consequently, with \(\operatorname{off}(G)=G-\operatorname{diag}(\operatorname{diag}(G))\), the symmetric matrix
\[
 C_\varepsilon
 =\operatorname{off}\!\left(Q_\varepsilon
 \operatorname{diag}(s_e)Q_\varepsilon^{\mathsf T}\right)
 \tag{25}
\]
is independent of the choice of \(e\in S\).  Define
\[
 \Omega'_\varepsilon
 =Q_\varepsilon\Omega Q_\varepsilon^{\mathsf T}+C_\varepsilon.
 \tag{26}
\]
This matrix is symmetric and depends continuously on \(\varepsilon\); at zero it equals \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_{++}^p\).  Openness of the positive-definite cone therefore permits a sufficiently small nonzero \(\varepsilon\) for which, simultaneously,
\[
 D'=D'_{\varepsilon}\in\mathcal D,
 \qquad D'\ne D,
 \qquad \Omega'=\Omega'_\varepsilon\in\mathbb S_{++}^p.
 \tag{27}
\]
For \(e\in S\) and \(1\le i\le p\), set
\[
 t_{ei}
 =[Q_\varepsilon\operatorname{diag}(s_e)Q_\varepsilon^{\mathsf T}]_{ii}
 =\sum_{j=1}^p(Q_\varepsilon)_{ij}^2s_{ej}\ge0,
 \tag{28}
\]
where the inequality uses \(\text{ass:nonnegative-shifts}\).  Equations (25)--(28) and \(\text{ass:honest-covariance-model}\) imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 D'\Sigma_eD'^{\mathsf T}
 &=Q_\varepsilon\bigl(\Omega+\operatorname{diag}(s_e)\bigr)Q_\varepsilon^{\mathsf T}\\
 &=\Omega'+\operatorname{diag}(t_e),
 \qquad e\in S.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{29}
\]
Let \(H'=S\cup(E\setminus H)\).  This union is disjoint and
\[
 |H'|=q+c=h.
 \tag{30}
\]
For every \(e\in E\setminus H\), assign
\[
 \Sigma_e=(D')^{-1}\Omega'(D')^{-\mathsf T}.
 \tag{31}
\]
These replacements are positive definite by (27) and invertible congruence.  Equations (28)--(31) show that \(D'\) fits every slot of \(H'\), with zero shifts on \(E\setminus H\), while \(D\) fits \(H\).  Thus \(D,D'\in\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)\), proving the fixed-interior-instance converse.

The published class permits \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_+^p\) and every positive-semidefinite covariance family, and it contains the strict subclass with \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_{++}^p\) and positive-definite covariances.  For any shift design with \(\delta_H\le c\), take, for example, \(D=I_p\) and \(\Omega=I_p\); then the preceding construction supplies positive-definite replacements and a second admissible structural matrix.  Thus a uniform guarantee over the published class fails below the threshold.  This proves minimax sharpness without asserting ambiguity for a preassigned singular \(\Omega\).  Finally, when \(c=0\), one has \(h=m\), and
\[
 \delta_H>0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 M_{k\ell}<h\ \text{for every }k<\ell.
\]
This is exactly the condition that no complete pairwise shift cloud is contained in an affine line.  Combining this observation with (14) and the fixed-interior converse proves the stated equivalence on the positive-definite invariant-noise interior.

statements.statement: Under the prespecified support pattern \(Z\) and absolutely continuous active amplitudes, simultaneously for every \(k<\ell\), \(M_{k\ell}=M_{k\ell}^{\mathrm{gen}}\) almost surely. Consequently, the pattern guarantees \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)=\{D\}\) uniformly for all admissible \(D\in\mathcal D\), all \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_{+}^{p}\), and every positive-semidefinite assignment to the \(c\) replacement slots if and only if, for every \(k<\ell\), \(\max\{n_{00}^{k\ell}+n_{10}^{k\ell},n_{00}^{k\ell}+n_{01}^{k\ell},n_{00}^{k\ell}+\mathbf 1\{n_{11}^{k\ell}>0\},\min(2,h)\}<h-c\). Failure of this inequality has an ambiguity witness with positive-definite invariant noise and positive-definite covariance slots; it is not a claim that every fixed singular boundary instance is ambiguous. In particular, any uniformly robustly identifying support pattern satisfies \(m\ge2c+3\), and this environment-count lower bound is attained by support patterns with no larger forced affine incidence.
statements.justification: The exact four-term formula turns a support hypergraph into a uniform published-class design threshold and exposes the unavoidable \(2c+3\) environment floor.
statements.gap: Existing generic-amplitude and sparse-shift results do not compute affine-line occupancy under whole-environment replacement or distinguish uniform class necessity from pointwise behavior at singular invariant-noise boundaries.
statements.consumer: Experimental planners can select intervention targets so the realized sparse design tolerates a prespecified number of arbitrary positive-semidefinite failed environments uniformly over the published second-moment class.
statements.proof_tex:
By \(\text{ass:support-factorization}\), for every \(e\in H\) and \(k<\ell\),
\[
 (s_{ek},s_{e\ell})
 =(Z_{ek}a_{ek},Z_{e\ell}a_{e\ell}).
 \tag{32}
\]
Apply \(\text{lem:generic-affine-occupancy}\) with \(I=H\), \(r=h\), \(Z^\circ=Z\), and \(a^\circ=a\).  Its absolute-continuity premise is exactly \(\text{ass:generic-active-amplitudes}\).  Hence, on one probability-one event and simultaneously for all \(k<\ell\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 M_{k\ell}
 &=\max\!\left\{
 n_{00}^{k\ell}+n_{10}^{k\ell},
 n_{00}^{k\ell}+n_{01}^{k\ell},
 n_{00}^{k\ell}+\mathbf 1\{n_{11}^{k\ell}>0\},
 \min(2,h)
 \right\}\\
 &=M_{k\ell}^{\mathrm{gen}}.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{33}
\]
This application counts indexed observations, so coincident zero-shift points contribute with their full multiplicity.

By \(\text{def:environment-distance}\),
\[
 \delta_H>c
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 M_{k\ell}<h-c\quad\text{for every }k<\ell.
 \tag{34}
\]
Substitution of (33) into (34) gives exactly the displayed four-term support criterion.  The factorization in \(\text{ass:support-factorization}\), together with \(Z_{ek}\in\{0,1\}\) and \(a_{ek}>0\), also verifies \(s_{ek}\ge0\), consistently with \(\text{ass:nonnegative-shifts}\).  If the criterion holds, the positive-semidefinite sufficiency part of \(\text{thm:sharp-replacement-radius}\), together with \(\text{ass:honest-covariance-model}\), proves \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)=\{D\}\) for every \(D\in\mathcal D\), every \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_+^p\), and every positive-semidefinite replacement assignment.  The probability-one event in (33) depends only on the amplitudes and support, so this conclusion is uniform over those structural and nuisance choices.

Conversely, if the support criterion fails, (33)--(34) give \(\delta_H\le c\).  Choose \(D=I_p\), which belongs to \(\mathcal D\) because it is invertible, has unit diagonal, and satisfies \(\operatorname{CP}(0)=0<1\), and choose \(\Omega=I_p\in\mathbb S_{++}^p\).  The honest covariances \(I_p+\operatorname{diag}(s_e)\) are positive definite.  The fixed-interior converse in \(\text{thm:sharp-replacement-radius}\) supplies positive-definite replacements and a second admissible structural matrix.  Therefore a uniform guarantee over the full positive-semidefinite class fails.  This proves necessity at the class level through its positive-definite subclass, without making a pointwise assertion at a singular invariant-noise boundary.

The term \(\min(2,h)\) makes the strict inequality in (34) possible only if \(h-c\ge3\).  Since \(h=m-c\), every uniformly robustly identifying support pattern must satisfy
\[
 m\ge2c+3.
 \tag{35}
\]
The bound is attained.  When \(m=2c+3\), choose the all-active pattern \(Z_{ek}=1\).  Then, for every \(k<\ell\),
\[
 n_{11}^{k\ell}=h,
 \qquad
 n_{00}^{k\ell}=n_{10}^{k\ell}=n_{01}^{k\ell}=0,
 \qquad
 M_{k\ell}^{\mathrm{gen}}=2<h-c=3.
 \tag{36}
\]
Thus all-active support attains the smallest possible environment count and has no forced affine incidence larger than the unavoidable two-point term.

statements.statement:
Let every covariance region be supplied by \(\text{def:encoded-covariance-regions}\), and let \(\gamma_0,\zeta_0,\lambda_0\in\mathbb Q_{>0}\) and \(\overline\kappa,\overline M\in\mathbb Q\) satisfy \(\overline\kappa,\overline M\geq1\). Under \(\text{ass:backshift-normalization}\), \(\text{ass:nonnegative-shifts}\), and \(\text{ass:honest-covariance-model}\), suppose additionally that \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_+^p\). For
\[
G_{n,\alpha,H}=\{\Sigma_e\in\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}\text{ for every }e\in H\},
\]
one has
\[
G_{n,\alpha,H}\subseteq\{D\in\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\}.
\]
Consequently, \(\Pr(G_{n,\alpha,H})\geq1-\alpha\) implies \(\Pr\{D\in\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\}\geq1-\alpha\).

Pointwise for every realized encoded region family, the procedure in \(\text{def:certificate-inference-handle}\) terminates. Its first quantifier-elimination output is a finite quantifier-free rational-polynomial formula whose realization is exactly the complete confidence union \(\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\). Its audit sentence is true exactly when there exists a full feasible candidate tuple whose affine separation, cycle slack, positive-definiteness margin, condition number, or scale violates, respectively, \(\gamma_0,\zeta_0,\lambda_0,\overline\kappa,\overline M\). Hence the procedure returns the exact full-union code after a clean universal audit and otherwise returns \(\mathsf{ABSTAIN}\). In particular, it abstains whenever a feasible candidate has zero affine separation.

The encoded input contract is essential for this exact symbolic conclusion in the finite-membership-query model: \(\text{lem:finite-membership-query-obstruction}\) gives rational positive-definite regions with separated affine minors for which no deterministic procedure using only finitely many membership queries computes the exact union for every arbitrary nonempty region family. No operator-norm contraction or confidence-union rate follows from this representation theorem; such a result additionally requires a proved inverse joint-diagonalization coercivity bound or a compact candidate envelope. The causal target remains \(B=I_p-D\), while \(\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\) is an observed-region compatibility functional whose coverage relation to that target is proved above rather than imposed by definition.
statements.justification: This supplies a terminating exact confidence-union code and a conservative, decidable margin-triggered abstention rule for finitely encoded rational-semialgebraic covariance regions, while proving finite-sample coverage under positive-semidefinite invariant noise.
statements.gap: The theorem does not establish operator-norm contraction. That separate analytic problem requires an inverse joint-diagonalization coercivity theorem or a compact candidate envelope and cannot be inferred from semialgebraic representability.
statements.consumer: A future corruption-aware BACKSHIFT implementation can enumerate candidate honest subsets, project the full feasibility formulas, and expose either the exact union code after a clean audit or an abstention; no CRAN implementation is claimed here.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Coverage under positive-semidefinite invariant noise.}
Fix \(n\geq1\), \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), and a sample outcome in \(G_{n,\alpha,H}\). For \(e\in H\), put \(\Gamma_e=\Sigma_e\). For each of the finitely many \(e\in E\setminus H\), choose \(\Gamma_e\in\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}\); such a choice exists because nonemptiness is part of \(\text{def:encoded-covariance-regions}\). Take
\[
A=D,\qquad K=H,\qquad \Psi=\Omega,\qquad t_e=s_e\quad(e\in H).
\]
The definition of \(H\) gives \(|K|=h\). Assumption \(\text{ass:backshift-normalization}\) gives \(A=D\in\mathcal D\). The theorem-local condition \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_+^p\) gives \(\Psi\in\mathbb S_+^p\), and \(\text{ass:nonnegative-shifts}\) gives \(t_e\in[0,\infty)^p\). Finally, membership in \(G_{n,\alpha,H}\) and \(\text{ass:honest-covariance-model}\) give, for every \(e\in K=H\),
\[
\Gamma_e=\Sigma_e
=D^{-1}\bigl(\Omega+\operatorname{diag}(s_e)\bigr)D^{-\mathsf T}
=A^{-1}\bigl(\Psi+\operatorname{diag}(t_e)\bigr)A^{-\mathsf T}.
\]
These are exactly the witnesses required by \(\text{def:compatible-set}\), so \(D\in\mathcal R_c(\Gamma)\). By \(\text{def:confidence-union}\), \(D\in\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\). This proves
\[
G_{n,\alpha,H}\subseteq\{D\in\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\}.
\]
Monotonicity of probability then gives
\[
\Pr\{D\in\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\}
\geq\Pr(G_{n,\alpha,H})\geq1-\alpha.
\]
Notice that this argument used only \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_+^p\), not \(\text{ass:invariant-noise-interior}\).

\textbf{The exact projected code.}
Fix a realized encoded family and abbreviate its rational formula by \(\rho_e(\Gamma_e)\). For a set \(K\subseteq E\) with \(|K|=h\), expand the formula \(F_K\) from \(\text{def:certificate-inference-handle}\). All matrix equalities are entrywise polynomial equalities. Invertibility is the polynomial inequality \((\det A)^2>0\). If \(\mathfrak C_p\) is the finite set of directed simple cycles of length at least two and \(\pi_C(A)\) is the product of the corresponding entries of \(I_p-A\), then
\[
\operatorname{CP}(I_p-A)<1
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
-1<\pi_C(A)<1\quad\text{for every }C\in\mathfrak C_p,
\]
by the definition of \(\operatorname{CP}\). The right side is expressed by \(1-\pi_C(A)>0\) and \(1+\pi_C(A)>0\). Positive semidefiniteness of the symmetric variable \(\Psi\) is, by the definition of that cone, the first-order condition
\[
\forall v\in\mathbb R^p,\qquad v^{\mathsf T}\Psi v\geq0.
\]
Positive definiteness of a symmetric \(\Gamma_e\) is likewise the first-order condition
\[
\forall v\in\mathbb R^p,\qquad
\left(\sum_{j=1}^p v_j^2=0\right)
\ \vee\ v^{\mathsf T}\Gamma_ev>0.
\]
The region atom \(\rho_e(\Gamma_e)\) is a finite Boolean combination of rational-polynomial signs by \(\text{def:encoded-covariance-regions}\). The remaining clauses \(A_{ii}=1\), \(t_{ej}\geq0\), and
\[
A\Gamma_eA^{\mathsf T}=\Psi+\operatorname{diag}(t_e)
\]
are polynomial conditions with integer coefficients. Hence \(F_K\) is a first-order ordered-field formula with rational-polynomial atoms and contains every feasibility requirement listed in the theorem.

Let
\[
\Phi_{\mathcal U}(A)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\bigvee_{\substack{K\subseteq E\\|K|=h}}
\exists\Psi\,\exists(t_e)_{e\in K}\,\exists(\Gamma_e)_{e\in K} F_K.
\]
We prove equality between its realization and \(\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\) in both directions. First suppose \(A\in\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\). By \(\text{def:confidence-union}\), there is a full family \(\Gamma\), with \(\Gamma_e\in\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}\) for every \(e\in E\), such that \(A\in\mathcal R_c(\Gamma)\). By \(\text{def:compatible-set}\), there are a set \(K_0\subseteq E\) with \(|K_0|\geq h\), a matrix \(\Psi\in\mathbb S_+^p\), and nonnegative shifts \(t_e\) satisfying the covariance equations on \(K_0\). Choose any \(K\subseteq K_0\) with \(|K|=h\). Restriction of these witnesses to \(K\) satisfies \(F_K\), so \(\Phi_{\mathcal U}(A)\) holds.

Conversely, suppose \(\Phi_{\mathcal U}(A)\) holds. A disjunct supplies \(K\) of size \(h\) and witnesses satisfying \(F_K\). The determinant clause permits multiplication of
\[
A\Gamma_eA^{\mathsf T}=\Psi+\operatorname{diag}(t_e)
\]
by \(A^{-1}\) and \(A^{-\mathsf T}\), yielding
\[
\Gamma_e=A^{-1}\bigl(\Psi+\operatorname{diag}(t_e)\bigr)A^{-\mathsf T}
\qquad(e\in K).
\]
The unit-diagonal, cycle, positive-semidefinite, and nonnegativity clauses therefore give \(A\in\mathcal R_c(\Gamma)\) on \(K\). For every \(e\notin K\), choose an arbitrary \(\Gamma_e\in\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}\), possible by nonemptiness; the values outside \(K\) do not enter the compatibility witness. Thus the completed family is among those in \(\text{def:confidence-union}\), and \(A\in\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\). We have proved
\[
\{A:\Phi_{\mathcal U}(A)\}=\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha.
\]
There are exactly \(\binom mh\) disjuncts. Applying \(\text{lem:effective-real-quantifier-elimination}\) to their finite disjunction terminates and returns an equivalent quantifier-free formula with rational-polynomial sign atoms. Its realization is therefore exactly the complete confidence union.

\textbf{Polynomial margin audit.}
It remains to show that the five candidate-margin tests in \(\text{def:certificate-inference-handle}\) are effective and exact. For \(e<f<g\) and \(k<\ell\), the affine minor \(\Delta^{k\ell}_{efg}(t)\) is a polynomial. When \(h-c\geq3\), the condition \(\gamma(w)\geq\gamma_0\) is exactly the finite Boolean formula
\[
\bigwedge_{1\leq k<\ell\leq p}
\ \bigwedge_{\substack{S\subseteq K\\|S|=h-c}}
\ \bigvee_{e<f<g\in S}
\left(\Delta^{k\ell}_{efg}(t)\geq\gamma_0
\ \vee\ -\Delta^{k\ell}_{efg}(t)\geq\gamma_0\right).
\]
This is precisely the expansion of the finite minimum--maximum defining \(\gamma(w)\). When \(h-c<3\), the condition is false because \(\gamma(w)=0<\gamma_0\). The cycle condition \(\zeta(w)\geq\zeta_0\) is exactly
\[
\bigwedge_{C\in\mathfrak C_p}
\left(\pi_C(A)\leq1-\zeta_0\right)
\wedge
\left(-\pi_C(A)\leq1-\zeta_0\right).
\]
The positive-definiteness condition \(\lambda(w)\geq\lambda_0\) is exactly
\[
\forall v\in\mathbb R^p,\quad
v^{\mathsf T}(\Psi-\lambda_0I_p)v\geq0,
\qquad
\forall e\in K\ \forall v\in\mathbb R^p,\qquad
v^{\mathsf T}(\Gamma_e-\lambda_0I_p)v\geq0,
\]
by the Rayleigh-quotient definition of the least eigenvalue.

For the condition number, define the first-order formula
\[
\mathsf{Cond}_{\overline\kappa}(A)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\exists q>0\ \forall v\in\mathbb R^p,\qquad
q\sum_jv_j^2\leq\sum_i(Av)_i^2
\leq\overline\kappa^2q\sum_jv_j^2.
\]
If it holds, the upper inequality gives \(\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\overline\kappa\sqrt q\). Applying the lower inequality to \(v=A^{-1}u\) gives \(\|A^{-1}u\|_2\leq q^{-1/2}\|u\|_2\), hence \(\|A^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq q^{-1/2}\) and \(\kappa(w)\leq\overline\kappa\). Conversely, if \(\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|A^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\overline\kappa\), set \(q=\|A^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}^{-2}>0\). The norm inequalities
\[
\|Av\|_2\leq\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|v\|_2,
\qquad
\|v\|_2=\|A^{-1}Av\|_2\leq\|A^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|Av\|_2
\]
give both clauses in \(\mathsf{Cond}_{\overline\kappa}(A)\). Thus this polynomial first-order formula is equivalent to the stated condition-number bound.

For scale, let \(\mathsf{NormBd}(X,r)\) abbreviate
\[
r\geq0\quad\wedge\quad
\forall v\in\mathbb R^p,\qquad
\sum_i(Xv)_i^2\leq r^2\sum_jv_j^2.
\]
By the definition of the operator norm, this is equivalent to \(\|X\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq r\). Therefore \(M(w)\leq\overline M\) is equivalent to existence of \(r_\Psi,r_\Gamma,r_t\geq0\) such that
\[
\begin{gathered}
\mathsf{NormBd}(\Psi,r_\Psi),\qquad
\mathsf{NormBd}(\Gamma_e,r_\Gamma)\quad(e\in K),\\
\mathsf{NormBd}(\operatorname{diag}(t_e),r_t)\quad(e\in K),
\qquad
1+r_\Psi+r_\Gamma+r_t\leq\overline M.
\end{gathered}
\]
Indeed, any such bounds dominate the three maxima in \(M(w)\); conversely one may choose the three actual maxima of the finitely many operator norms. This is again a first-order rational-polynomial formula.

All threshold coefficients are rational by hypothesis. Hence the sentence
\[
\mathsf{Bad}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\bigvee_{\substack{K\subseteq E\\|K|=h}}
\exists A\,\exists\Psi\,\exists t\,\exists\Gamma_K
\left[F_K\wedge\neg\mathsf{Good}(w)
\right],
\]
where \(\mathsf{Good}(w)\) is the conjunction of the five displayed margin conditions, is a closed first-order formula over rational polynomial signs. By \(\text{lem:effective-real-quantifier-elimination}\), its truth is decidable in finite time. It is false exactly when every feasible candidate satisfies every threshold. Thus the procedure returns the already-computed exact union code exactly after a clean universal audit and returns \(\mathsf{ABSTAIN}\) otherwise. If a feasible tuple has \(\gamma(w)=0\), then \(\gamma_0>0\) makes \(\mathsf{Good}(w)\) false, so \(\mathsf{Bad}\) is true and the procedure abstains.

The finite-membership-query necessity clause is exactly \(\text{lem:finite-membership-query-obstruction}\), which the present theorem consumes only to justify the encoded input contract. No step above supplies an inverse perturbation inequality for joint diagonalization, and no bounded candidate envelope was assumed; accordingly the proof establishes no contraction assertion. Finally, \(B=I_p-D\) is fixed as the causal structural target independently of the observed-region set \(\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\). The first part derives the advertised coverage relation between them.

statements.statement: Every first-order formula over the ordered field of real numbers whose atomic predicates are sign conditions on finitely many polynomials with rational coefficients admits an effectively computable equivalent quantifier-free formula.  In particular, closed such formulas are decidable, and projections of rational semialgebraic sets have computable rational semialgebraic descriptions.

statements.statement:
Let \(I\) be a finite index set of cardinality \(r\), let \(Z^\circ\in\{0,1\}^{I\times p}\), and let \(a^\circ\in(0,\infty)^{I\times p}\). Suppose the subarray \((a^\circ_{ek}:Z^\circ_{ek}=1)\) has a joint distribution absolutely continuous on its positive orthant. Define \(P_e^{k\ell}=(Z^\circ_{ek}a^\circ_{ek},Z^\circ_{e\ell}a^\circ_{e\ell})\), \(N_{uv}^{k\ell}=\#\{e\in I:(Z^\circ_{ek},Z^\circ_{e\ell})=(u,v)\}\), and \(M_I^{k\ell}=\max_{L\text{ affine line}}\#\{e\in I:P_e^{k\ell}\in L\}\). Then, simultaneously for all \(k<\ell\), almost surely
\[
 M_I^{k\ell}=\max\{N_{00}^{k\ell}+N_{10}^{k\ell},N_{00}^{k\ell}+N_{01}^{k\ell},N_{00}^{k\ell}+\mathbf 1\{N_{11}^{k\ell}>0\},\min(2,r)\}.
\]
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(k<\ell\) and abbreviate \(P_e^{k\ell}=(x_e,y_e)\).  Type \(00\) gives the origin, types \(10\) and \(01\) give the two positive coordinate axes, and type \(11\) gives the open positive quadrant.  The horizontal axis, vertical axis, a line through the origin and one type \(11\) point when such a point exists, and a line through any two indexed points show
\[
 M_I^{k\ell}\ge
 \max\!\left\{
 N_{00}^{k\ell}+N_{10}^{k\ell},
 N_{00}^{k\ell}+N_{01}^{k\ell},
 N_{00}^{k\ell}+\mathbf 1\{N_{11}^{k\ell}>0\},
 \min(2,r)
 \right\}. \tag{22}
\]

For two nonzero-support points, collinearity with the origin is the polynomial equation
\[
 x_ey_f-x_fy_e=0. \tag{23}
\]
Unless both types are \(10\), or both are \(01\), this polynomial is not identically zero in the active coordinates: the mixed axis and axis--interior cases contain a nonzero product, while the interior--interior case contains two distinct monomials.  For three nonzero-support points, collinearity is the equation
\[
 \det\!\begin{pmatrix}
 1&x_e&y_e\\
 1&x_f&y_f\\
 1&x_g&y_g
 \end{pmatrix}=0. \tag{24}
\]
Except when all three types are \(10\), or all three are \(01\), this is not the zero polynomial.  To verify this, choose two distinct horizontal points and a vertical or interior point, use the coordinate-swapped construction, put one point off the line through the other two in the remaining mixed cases, and use \((1,1),(1,2),(2,1)\) for three interior points.  Equality of the active coordinates of two distinct type \(10\) points, and its type \(01\) analogue, is also the zero set of a nonzero linear polynomial.

The zero set of a nonzero polynomial in finitely many real variables has Lebesgue measure zero.  An induction proves this directly: a nonzero univariate polynomial has finitely many roots; after expansion in the last variable, the induction hypothesis removes the null set on which all coefficient polynomials vanish, every remaining section has finitely many roots, and integration of the null sections gives the result.  There are finitely many coordinate pairs and indexed pairs and triples.  Joint absolute continuity therefore gives a single probability-one event on which none of the non-forced equations (23)--(24) or coordinate equalities occurs, simultaneously for all \(k<\ell\).

On that event, a line through the origin containing type \(10\) is the horizontal axis, and the coordinate-swapped statement holds for type \(01\).  A line through the origin containing neither axis type has at most one type \(11\) point by (23).  A line not through the origin has no type \(00\) point; if it contained three indices, (24) would force all three to be type \(10\) or all three to be type \(01\), but the resulting coordinate axis passes through the origin.  Thus every line is bounded by one of the four quantities in (22), proving equality.
statements.justification: This finite-index lemma isolates the generic incidence calculation so both realized-set and ex-ante full-array design results use the same declared proof spine.
statements.gap: Sparse-support results do not provide this exact affine-line occupancy formula with repeated origin points and two forced coordinate axes.
statements.consumer: The full-array deletion-radius corollary applies the lemma before taking the worst retained subset.

statements.statement: Let \(\bar Z\in\{0,1\}^{E\times p}\) be a planned full-environment support array and let \(\bar a\in(0,\infty)^{E\times p}\). Suppose the active subarray \((\bar a_{ek}:\bar Z_{ek}=1)\) has a joint density on its positive orthant, and put \(\bar s_{ek}=\bar Z_{ek}\bar a_{ek}\). For \(u,v\in\{0,1\}\), define \(N_{uv}^{k\ell}=\#\{e\in E:(\bar Z_{ek},\bar Z_{e\ell})=(u,v)\}\), and set \(T=\max_{k<\ell}\max\{N_{00}^{k\ell}+N_{10}^{k\ell},N_{00}^{k\ell}+N_{01}^{k\ell},N_{00}^{k\ell}+\mathbf 1\{N_{11}^{k\ell}>0\},\min(2,m)\}\). Almost surely, the following are equivalent: (i) for every failed set \(F\subseteq E\) with \(|F|=c\), the retained set \(H=E\setminus F\) and shifts \((\bar s_e:e\in H)\) give a design that guarantees \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)=\{D\}\) uniformly over all admissible \(D\in\mathcal D\), all \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_+^p\), and all positive-semidefinite replacements; (ii) \(T<m-2c\). If \(T<m\), condition (ii) is equivalent to \(c\le\lfloor(m-T-1)/2\rfloor\); if \(T=m\), no nonnegative corruption budget is certified. For the all-active design and \(m\ge3\), the largest certified budget is \(c_{\max}=\lfloor(m-3)/2\rfloor\).
statements.justification: This corollary converts the realized honest-set radius into an ex-ante guarantee against every choice of failed environments.
statements.gap: The realized-design occupancy formula alone does not tell a planner whether every possible deletion set remains safe; the full-array statistic \(T\) closes that quantifier exactly.
statements.consumer: An experimental planner computes \(T\) once and certifies every \(c\)-environment failure set exactly when \(T<m-2c\), before collecting outcomes.
statements.proof_tex:
For a coordinate pair \(k<\ell\), let
\[
 T_{k\ell}
 =\max\!\left\{
 N_{00}^{k\ell}+N_{10}^{k\ell},
 N_{00}^{k\ell}+N_{01}^{k\ell},
 N_{00}^{k\ell}+\mathbf 1\{N_{11}^{k\ell}>0\},
 \min(2,m)
 \right\},
\]
so that \(T=\max_{k<\ell}T_{k\ell}\).  Apply \(\text{lem:generic-affine-occupancy}\) with \(I=E\), \(r=m\), \(Z^\circ=\bar Z\), and \(a^\circ=\bar a\).  Its absolute-continuity premise is the stated joint-density premise.  Hence, on one probability-one event and simultaneously for every pair, the full \((k,\ell)\)-cloud has maximum indexed affine-line occupancy \(T_{k\ell}\).

Fix \(k<\ell\).  For a retained set \(H\subseteq E\) of size \(m-c\), write \(M_{k\ell}(H)\) for the maximum line occupancy after restriction to \(H\).  Then
\[
 \max_{H\subseteq E:\,|H|=m-c}M_{k\ell}(H)
 =\min\{T_{k\ell},m-c\}.
 \tag{37}
\]
Indeed, restriction cannot increase the full occupancy and a retained set has only \(m-c\) indices, proving the upper bound.  For the reverse bound, choose a line attaining the full occupancy \(T_{k\ell}\).  If \(T_{k\ell}\ge m-c\), retain any \(m-c\) indexed points on that line.  If \(T_{k\ell}<m-c\), retain all its \(T_{k\ell}\) indices and add any \(m-c-T_{k\ell}\) other indices.  These two constructions prove (37).

For every retained set, \(h=m-c\).  The class-uniform consequence of \(\text{thm:sharp-replacement-radius}\) says that this retained design guarantees recovery for all positive-semidefinite invariant nuisances and all positive-semidefinite replacements if and only if
\[
 M_{k\ell}(H)<h-c=m-2c
 \quad\text{for every }k<\ell.
 \tag{38}
\]
For clarity, sufficiency in this equivalence is the theorem's positive-semidefinite conclusion.  If (38) fails, choosing \(D=I_p\) and \(\Omega=I_p\) lets the theorem's fixed-interior converse provide a positive-definite replacement assignment witnessing failure of the class-uniform guarantee.

Since \(m-2c\le m-c\), equation (37) implies
\[
 \min\{T_{k\ell},m-c\}<m-2c
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 T_{k\ell}<m-2c.
 \tag{39}
\]
The choices of retained set and coordinate pair range over finite sets, so their universal quantifiers may be interchanged.  Equations (37)--(39) therefore show that (38) holds for every retained set if and only if
\[
 T_{k\ell}<m-2c\quad\text{for every }k<\ell,
\]
which is equivalent to \(T<m-2c\).

Because \(c\) is an integer, when \(T<m\) this strict inequality is equivalent to
\[
 2c\le m-T-1
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 c\le\left\lfloor\frac{m-T-1}{2}\right\rfloor.
 \tag{40}
\]
If \(T=m\), even \(c=0\) violates the strict inequality, so no nonnegative corruption budget is certified.  For the all-active design, \(N_{11}^{k\ell}=m\) and \(N_{00}^{k\ell}=N_{10}^{k\ell}=N_{01}^{k\ell}=0\), so \(T=2\) whenever \(m\ge2\).  In particular, for \(m\ge3\), (40) gives
\[
 c_{\max}=\left\lfloor\frac{m-3}{2}\right\rfloor,
\]
as claimed.

statements.statement: For \(p=2\), \(m=h=3\), and \(c=0\), there are rational matrices \(\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2,\Sigma_3\in\mathbb S_{++}^2\) whose BACKSHIFT compatibility set is \(\mathcal R_0(\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2,\Sigma_3)=\{I_2\}\) and whose shift profiles have affine separation \(\gamma_H=1\), together with infinitely many pairwise distinct rational matrices \(\Gamma_{3,q}\in\mathbb S_{++}^2\) and matrices \(A_q\in\mathcal D\setminus\{I_2\}\) satisfying \(A_q\in\mathcal R_0(\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2,\Gamma_{3,q})\). Consequently, no deterministic procedure that has only membership-oracle access to arbitrary nonempty covariance regions and makes finitely many membership queries can compute, for every such region family, the exact set-theoretic confidence union obtained by taking the union of \(\mathcal R_0\) over the regions.
statements.justification: This explicit indistinguishable-oracle witness proves that finite membership access cannot support exact confidence-union computation for arbitrary nonempty matrix regions, even away from zero affine separation.
statements.gap: The lemma is specific to the membership-oracle information model and does not obstruct exact computation from finite rational-semialgebraic codes.
statements.consumer: The constructive inference theorem uses this lemma to justify its encoded-region input contract without substituting the obstruction for the promised construction.
statements.proof_tex:
Take
\[
\Sigma_1=\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\0&2\end{pmatrix},\qquad
\Sigma_2=\begin{pmatrix}3&0\\0&2\end{pmatrix},\qquad
\Sigma_3=\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\0&3\end{pmatrix}.
\]
All three matrices are rational and positive definite because their diagonal entries are positive. They arise with \(D=I_2\), \(\Omega=2I_2\), and shifts \(s_1=(0,0)\), \(s_2=(1,0)\), \(s_3=(0,1)\). Direct expansion gives
\[
\gamma_H=
\left|\det\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\1&1&0\\1&0&1\end{pmatrix}\right|=1.
\]

Let \(A\in\mathcal R_0(\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2,\Sigma_3)\). Since \(h=m=3\), \(\text{def:compatible-set}\) forces the compatible subset to be all three environments. Unit diagonal gives
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}1&x\\y&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Subtracting the transformed covariance equation at environment one from those at environments two and three cancels the common invariant matrix. The differences must be diagonal, while direct multiplication gives
\[
A(\Sigma_2-\Sigma_1)A^{\mathsf T}
=\begin{pmatrix}1&y\\y&y^2\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
A(\Sigma_3-\Sigma_1)A^{\mathsf T}
=\begin{pmatrix}x^2&x\\x&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Their off-diagonal entries imply \(y=0\) and \(x=0\). Thus \(A=I_2\). Conversely, \(I_2\) is compatible with invariant matrix \(2I_2\) and the displayed nonnegative shifts, so
\[
\mathcal R_0(\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2,\Sigma_3)=\{I_2\}.
\]

For each nonzero \(q\in\mathbb Q\), set
\[
A_q=\begin{pmatrix}1&q\\0&1\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\Psi_q=2\begin{pmatrix}1+q^2&q\\q&1\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\Gamma_{3,q}=\begin{pmatrix}2+q^2&-q\\-q&3\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The matrix \(A_q\) is invertible and has unit diagonal. The two-cycle product of \(I_2-A_q\) is zero, so \(A_q\in\mathcal D\). For every nonzero vector \(v\),
\[
v^{\mathsf T}\Psi_qv=2\|A_q^{\mathsf T}v\|_2^2>0,
\]
because \(A_q\) is invertible. If \(v=(u,w)^{\mathsf T}\neq0\), then
\[
v^{\mathsf T}\Gamma_{3,q}v
=2u^2+(qu-w)^2+2w^2>0.
\]
Thus both \(\Psi_q\) and \(\Gamma_{3,q}\) are positive definite. Direct multiplication yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
A_q\Sigma_1A_q^{\mathsf T}&=\Psi_q,\\
A_q\Sigma_2A_q^{\mathsf T}&=\Psi_q+\operatorname{diag}(1,0),\\
A_q\Gamma_{3,q}A_q^{\mathsf T}&=\Psi_q+\operatorname{diag}(0,1).
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore \(A_q\in\mathcal R_0(\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2,\Gamma_{3,q})\). Since \(q\neq0\), \(A_q\neq I_2\). The matrices \(\Gamma_{3,q}\) are pairwise distinct because their off-diagonal entry is \(-q\).

Suppose, for contradiction, that a deterministic finite-membership-query procedure computes the exact union for every arbitrary nonempty region family. Run it on the singleton regions
\[
\mathcal C^0_1=\{\Sigma_1\},\qquad
\mathcal C^0_2=\{\Sigma_2\},\qquad
\mathcal C^0_3=\{\Sigma_3\}.
\]
Its required output is \(\{I_2\}\). Only finitely many matrices are queried from the third oracle. Since the family \((\Gamma_{3,q}:q\in\mathbb Q\setminus\{0\})\) is infinite and pairwise distinct, choose \(q\neq0\) for which \(\Gamma_{3,q}\) was not queried. Replace only the third region by
\[
\mathcal C^1_3=\{\Sigma_3,\Gamma_{3,q}\}.
\]
Induction over the query number shows that the two runs have identical transcripts. Initially their internal states agree. If their transcripts agree before a query, determinism selects the same region and matrix. Answers from the first two oracles agree because those regions are unchanged. Answers from the third agree along the original transcript because membership differs only at the unqueried point \(\Gamma_{3,q}\). Hence the next internal states also agree. The original run terminates after finitely many queries, so the modified run terminates with the same output \(\{I_2\}\).

But the modified exact union contains \(A_q\), because
\[
A_q\in\mathcal R_0(\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2,\Gamma_{3,q}),
\]
whereas \(A_q\notin\{I_2\}\). This contradiction proves the finite-membership-query obstruction. The witness consists entirely of rational positive-definite matrices and has \(\gamma_H=1\), so the obstruction is about input representation rather than vanishing affine separation.

statements.statement: Using \(\text{CertificateInferenceHandle}\), can one construct finite rational affine-minor certificates for singleton, multiple-candidate, and infeasible population outputs when every \(\Sigma_e\) is rational, together with a computable implementation of \(\mathcal U^{(n)}_{\alpha}\) that retains the definition-level coverage implication: every indexed region family having simultaneous honest-slot coverage probability at least \(1-\alpha\) yields \(\Pr\{D\in\mathcal U^{(n)}_{\alpha}\}\ge1-\alpha\)? Quantitatively, can one give explicit functions \(r_0(\gamma_H,\kappa_D,\zeta_D,\lambda_H,M_H,p,m)>0\) and \(C(\gamma_H^{-1},\kappa_D,\zeta_D^{-1},\lambda_H^{-1},M_H,p,m)\in(0,\infty)\) such that, for every \(n\ge1\) and \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), on the simultaneous honest-slot coverage event and whenever \(r_{n,\alpha,H}\le r_0\), \(\operatorname{outer}_{\mathrm{op}}(\mathcal U^{(n)}_{\alpha},D)\le C r_{n,\alpha,H}\), and hence \(\operatorname{diam}_{\mathrm{op}}(\mathcal U^{(n)}_{\alpha})\le2C r_{n,\alpha,H}\)? The coverage implication and inequalities must hold uniformly over classes with fixed \(p,m,c\) and bounds \(\gamma_H\ge\gamma_0>0\), \(\zeta_D\ge\zeta_0>0\), \(\lambda_H\ge\lambda_0>0\), \(\kappa_D\le\overline\kappa\), and \(M_H\le\overline M\). The contraction conclusion \(\operatorname{outer}_{\mathrm{op}}(\mathcal U^{(n)}_{\alpha},D)\to0\) and \(\operatorname{diam}_{\mathrm{op}}(\mathcal U^{(n)}_{\alpha})\to0\) is required only along region sequences satisfying \(r_{n,\alpha,H}\to0\). Can normalization charts be switched without invalidating the certificates? Separately, whenever the simultaneous regions admit a compatible BACKSHIFT explanation with \(\gamma_H=0\), can the implementation be required to return the full set-valued feasible output or abstain rather than report a singleton?
statements.justification: The unresolved mathematical content is a checkable algebraic certificate and a quantitative modulus that remains honest at the affine-identification boundary.
statements.gap: Afsari2008JDSensitivity gives local sensitivity for an already selected approximate diagonalization problem, and AndrewsCheng2013SporadicID gives general identification-robust inference; neither handles subset changes, BACKSHIFT normalization, or rational affine-minor certificates.
statements.consumer: A production backShift implementation can abstain near weak identification while issuing shrinking confidence sets under explicitly certified separation and conditioning.

sampling_model.design: There are \(m\) labeled environments; an unknown set \(H\) of size \(h=m-c\) follows one population BACKSHIFT covariance model and the remaining \(c\) slots are arbitrary elements of \(\mathbb S_{++}^{p}\).
sampling_model.units: For population identification only \(\Sigma_e\) is observed. At each index \(n\), every slot supplies an independent within-environment sample of size \(n\) used to construct the indexed simultaneous covariance region \(\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}\).
sampling_model.treatment: Unknown additive shift interventions have diagonal covariance \(\operatorname{diag}(s_e)\); intervention targets and strengths are not observed.
sampling_model.overlap: The two candidate honest subsets may overlap in only \(m-2c=h-c\) slots.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nuisance is estimated for the population theorem. Compatibility permits an invariant nuisance in \(\mathbb S_{+}^{p}\); the sharp converse and conditioning analysis impose the explicit interior condition \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_{++}^{p}\). The inference layer propagates indexed honest-slot simultaneous covariance regions through feasibility-oracle constraint inversion and measures all perturbations in operator norm.

estimand_functional: For a fixed honest design \(D,H,s\) and \(\Sigma\in(\mathbb S_+^p)^E\), let robust recovery mean that \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)=\{D\}\) for every positive-semidefinite assignment to the \(c\) slots in \(E\setminus H\). For every \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_+^p\), \(\delta_H>c\) implies robust recovery without an invertibility condition on the honest covariances. If the fixed instance has \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_{++}^p\), robust recovery holds if and only if \(\delta_H>c\), and failure is realized by positive-definite replacements. Thus \(\delta_H>c\) is minimax sharp over the published positive-semidefinite covariance and invariant-noise class, with failure witnessed in its positive-definite subclass.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The population BACKSHIFT solution is unique exactly when every pair of intervention-variance profiles is noncollinear.
An exact non-unitary joint diagonalizer is essentially unique if and only if the diagonal-profile collinearity modulus is below one.
Outlier target matrices are omitted by iteratively retaining matrices whose geometric residual is below a chosen threshold.

Theorem 1 gives noiseless unique topology identification when the exogenous-covariance factor has Kruskal rank at least two, nonzero edges are continuously distributed, and at least two off-diagonal nonzero entries are known in every column.
Simultaneous diagonalizability by congruence of a complete Hermitian family is equivalent to positive-definite feasibility of a linear matrix system.
Pairwise environment comparisons identify causal structure with high probability under probabilistically sparse mechanism changes.
Identification-robust tests and confidence sets maintain uniform asymptotic size across weak and strong identification regimes.

tldr: Unknown shift interventions identify a cyclic linear causal system because covariance differences share a non-unitary congruence diagonalizer. The field-tier kernel asks how many entire covariance environments may instead be arbitrary. The structural matrix satisfying the BACKSHIFT unit-diagonal and cycle-product normalization survives every \(c\)-slot positive-definite replacement if and only if deleting the largest affine-line subset from every pairwise honest shift cloud costs more than \(c\) environments. The converse uses the explicit interior condition on invariant noise to produce a legal positive-definite contamination and a second cycle-product-normalized system. A generic sparse-support formula turns the distance into a combinatorial design criterion; finite subset enumeration is only a reduction to an exact feasibility oracle, while operator-norm contraction of indexed confidence unions, rational certificates, and mandatory abstention at zero affine separation remain the computational agenda for updating the CRAN pooled-difference workflow.

project_justification.gap: Published BACKSHIFT identifies from an entirely honest environment family, general joint-diagonalization theory studies one complete matrix family, and existing outlier-aware joint diagonalization uses a tuning threshold without an exact adversarial radius.
project_justification.niche: Whole-environment replacement creates a discrete overlap geometry: two explanations may discard different slots and therefore share only \(m-2c\) covariance matrices. Affine rather than linear collinearity is the invariant obstruction because the common nondiagonal noise covariance disappears only after differencing.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the necessary-and-sufficient distance \(\delta_H>c\), a matching positive-definite contamination witness satisfying the BACKSHIFT cycle-product normalization under the interior-noise condition, and the exact generic support-incidence formula. Finite subset enumeration is recorded only as a definitional feasibility-oracle implementation note. The open inference target asks for explicit operator-norm radius and modulus functions for indexed confidence unions on fixed-margin uniform classes, rational certificates, chart switching, and abstention at vanishing affine minors.

related_work: The field-tier radius result is informed by RothenhauslerEtAl2015BackShift, Theorem 1 and its appendix proof, which supplies the all-honest model, pairwise profile reduction, and cycle-product normalization; its generic-amplitude result is Corollary 2(ii). KleinsteuberShen2013NUJDUniqueness, Theorem 1, informs the complete-family uniqueness step through profile collinearity. AkhavanEtAl2019GeometryJD, Section 4.2 and equation (42), informs the robust joint-diagonalization setting by trimming outlier target matrices with a chosen residual threshold, but it does not state a worst-case replacement radius. ShenEtAl2020RJDSEM, Section III.C and equations (27)--(28), defines R-JDSEM through an elementwise \(\ell_1\) joint-diagonalization loss for sparse node- or entry-level outlier components within local covariance matrices, rather than replacement of whole covariance slabs. Its noiseless anchored or known-edge Theorem 1 establishes a sufficient uniqueness result under prior edge information; it gives neither an adversarial whole-environment replacement radius, the criterion \(\delta_H>c\), nor a legal two-explanation BACKSHIFT converse. PerryVonKugelgenScholkopf2022SparseShift, Corollary 4.2, Theorem 5.3, and Corollary 5.4, shows how pairwise environment comparisons and sparse mechanism changes support detection and graph recovery, while PfisterPeters2022SparseIV, Theorem 3, illustrates how a support pattern can control generic causal identifiability. LeNguyen2022HermitianSDC, Theorem 7 and Algorithm 5, supplies a complete-family congruence-feasibility primitive; this proposal uses it only to motivate an oracle reduction and does not claim a terminating exact solver. Afsari2008JDSensitivity relates local joint-diagonalization error to conditioning and a uniqueness modulus.
